description: email.rs lines 563-573: the variable pair (limit, client_limit) encodes 'server-applied limit vs. what the client asked for' but the names do not make this clear. client_limit = None means the client omitted the field; limit is the clamped value actually used. The subsequent check 'if client_limit \!= Some(limit)' is correct but reads as a riddle. Suggested rewrite: name them (effective_limit, requested_limit) and the check becomes 'if requested_limit \!= Some(effective_limit)', which reads as the spec clause it implements: echo limit back when the server applied a cap different from what the client sent.
title: handle_email_query: (limit, client_limit) tuple obscures intent
